rules.name: arrays-meet-at-one-width
rules.statement: arrays that meet, as the operands of a method or the values of a condition, and give an array, or that one is looked up in, must be of one width, which must be known: Polars refuses to add arrays of two widths or to look one up in the other, and gives a list where it fills one with the other or takes one for a value of a condition and the other for another

rules.name: condition-predicate-is-boolean
rules.statement: a condition's predicate must be Boolean

rules.name: duration-is-valid
rules.statement: a duration typed in must be a duration string Polars reads

rules.name: element-dtype-is-implemented
rules.statement: a method of lists and arrays must be given an element dtype that Polars implements it for: it panics for the others where the rows run, on a thread of its own that its streaming executor may not recover from

rules.name: element-dtype-is-measured
rules.statement: a method whose answer depends on the element dtype of a list or an array must be given one the tables measure it on, the whole numbers, the floats, text, booleans, dates and datetimes: Polars is not asked of another, which it may panic on

rules.name: element-only-in-pivot-aggregate
rules.statement: `polars.element` stands only in a pivot's aggregate

rules.name: field-is-of-the-struct
rules.statement: a field that a method reads or drops must be one of the fields of the struct it follows: Polars refuses a name that is none, as one that was renamed or dropped before is

rules.name: field-names-fit-the-struct
rules.statement: the names given to the fields of a struct must be as many as its fields where it is renamed, or as the places of the array it is made of, and no two fields of a struct may be named alike: Polars refuses names of another number and two fields of one name

rules.name: filter-predicate-is-boolean
rules.statement: a filter's predicate must be Boolean

rules.name: folded-function-is-no-join-key
rules.statement: a moment or a length of time made of numbers typed in is folded by Polars into a literal named by an alias, which a join's key may not hold: give it a column among its parts, or make it in a step before the join

rules.name: grouped-names-are-distinct
rules.statement: the columns a group by gives must be named differently: a key is named by the column it reads or the name it is given, an aggregate by the column its chain reads or the name it is given, and Polars refuses two that are named alike, as a key and an aggregate of the same column are

rules.name: having-casts-to-boolean
rules.statement: a having's predicate must be a value Polars casts to a Boolean to keep a group or not: a Boolean, a number, or null where it stands alone, and not text, a date, a list or a struct, which it refuses when it runs the rows; beside another predicate, which Polars combines it with as the predicates of a filter are, it must be a Boolean

rules.name: having-gives-one-value
rules.statement: a having's predicate must give one value for each group: the values of the group, as a column or a method that keeps some of them gives, are a list that Polars cannot cast to a Boolean when it runs the rows, so give an aggregate such as the sum, the first value, whether all are true, or a count compared with a number

rules.name: is-in-takes-a-list
rules.statement: is_in must be given a list or an array to look the value up in, or a collection imploded, and not a collection nested as deeply as the value it follows, as a column of its own dtype is: Polars deprecates that form as ambiguous (pola-rs/polars#22149) and panics on one value looked up in another, so give a list, or the collection imploded

rules.name: join-key-names-are-not-repeated
rules.statement: a join may not pair the same two output column names twice: where two keys on one side are named alike, the keys they are paired with must be named differently

rules.name: kept-order-needs-keys-of-the-rows
rules.statement: where `maintain_order` keeps the order of the groups, a key must give one value or as many as the table has rows: Polars refuses a key that takes some of the values, as head, filter and drop_nulls do, for lengths that differ where the arguments or the data make it fewer, so give the key as a column, or leave the order unset

rules.name: key-is-elementwise
rules.statement: a join's key, and the key of a window in what a group by evaluates in `agg` or `having`, must be elementwise: an aggregate may not stand in it beside a column, nor a method that takes some of the values, as head and filter do, unless it goes on to an aggregate, nor a column be compared with a null, nor a column of whole numbers be compared for missing values with a literal that is a number with a fraction or a whole number its dtype cannot hold, as Polars reads the literal (a literal of 16 bit floats or of Boolean, and a float that does not cast exactly, are kept), nor a replacement take a value that reads a column

rules.name: literal-beside-values-in-a-group
rules.statement: in `agg` and `having`, a literal that dt.replace, str.splitn or str.split_exact maps may not be given the values of the group beside it (in a `having` only where it stands beside another value), nor one value that an aggregate gave in a `having`, a literal that sort_by sorts by them may not stand alone, and a literal that replace, replace_strict, str.replace or str.replace_all replaces may not be given either: Polars cannot replace a literal by values for each row, and refuses the map of one value beside many as of another length

rules.name: moments-share-a-zone
rules.statement: moments that are compared, subtracted, filled, bound by one another, or given as the values of a condition or as a replacement's new values and default, must be in one time zone: Polars finds no dtype that two zones have in common, and fails where a shift is filled with a moment of another zone

rules.name: one-column-is-needed
rules.statement: a filter's only predicate must be one column: an expression that gives several, as the unnest of a struct of several fields does, is ambiguous, and one that gives none, as the unnest of a struct of no field does, is empty, and Polars refuses both; beside another predicate each expression it expands to is a predicate of its own, which it takes

rules.name: parameter-takes-one-value
rules.statement: a parameter that Polars reads as one value must be given one: not the rows, nor a count of values that the data or the arguments decide, and, for the count of rows that `shift` and `diff` look back by and the value `shift` fills with, not the one value that a method took of one value either, which Polars cannot tell is one before the rows run

rules.name: pattern-is-valid
rules.statement: a pattern must be a valid regular expression

rules.name: pivot-aggregate-gives-one-value
rules.statement: a pivot's aggregate must give one value for each group

rules.name: range-is-valid
rules.statement: a range or a repeat typed in must be one Polars can make and cut: a step other than nothing, an interval above nothing that its bounds are read in, bounds the dtype holds, a number of values that is not below nothing, and, of it, no length below nothing to cut any value by

rules.name: replacement-values-match-in-number
rules.statement: a replacement takes as many new values as old ones, or one, and a strict one a default of as many values as what it follows, or one

rules.name: struct-arithmetic-needs-numbers
rules.statement: arithmetic with a struct needs its fields to be numbers: Polars refuses the absolute value, the negation, the sign, a clip and a power of a struct whatever its fields are, and the sum, the difference, the product and the quotients of one that has a field of text, a date, a moment or a time

rules.name: struct-is-filled-forward-or-backward
rules.statement: a struct is filled by a strategy only forward or backward: Polars refuses the smallest, the largest, the mean, zero and one where the struct holds a null, which a pivot's missing cells make, and does nothing where it holds none

rules.name: time-zone-is-valid
rules.statement: a time zone must be one Polars reads

rules.name: to-struct-names-are-distinct
rules.statement: no two names given to the fields of a struct that a list or an array is made may be alike: Polars 2.2.0 accepts them and builds a struct that disagrees with itself, as its dtype and its series hold two fields of one name, and refuses the same names for a struct made of columns or renamed

rules.name: values-meet-in-count
rules.statement: the values a call meets must be one value, which meets each of the others, or as many as one another: a count of values that the data or the arguments decide, as the first values of a column or the values that differ are, is not the table's rows and not another count it is not known to equal

rules.name: window-input-is-not-counted
rules.statement: a window takes a value as long as its group, and a count of values that the data or the arguments decide is not, nor is the one value that a method took of one value, unless the window joins the values of a group into a list or explodes them

rules.name: window-input-is-not-widened
rules.statement: a window takes a value as long as its input, and a value of one row that a part widens, as dt.replace's parts do, is not: Polars refuses the length of its output

rules.name: written-names-are-distinct
rules.statement: the columns that the items of a select or of with_columns write must be named differently: an unnest and a field read write the names of the fields, and Polars refuses two items that write one name

notKnown.name: the-starts-dtype
notKnown.because: the dtype of the start is not given

notKnown.name: the-results-dtype
notKnown.because: the dtype that the arguments decide is not known

notKnown.name: the-fields-of-a-struct
notKnown.because: the fields of the struct are not known, so whether the names the call reads, drops or renames are fields of it cannot be said

notKnown.name: an-unnest-as-a-key
notKnown.because: an unnest as a join's key writes a column for each field, and how many keys the other table expands to is not known

notKnown.name: an-unnest-of-no-field
notKnown.because: an unnest of a struct that has no field expands to no expression, which Polars leaves out or decides by its siblings

notKnown.name: an-open-number-in-a-key
notKnown.because: a number typed without a dtype stays open in a struct that is a join's key, as `dyn float` in its dtype, which Polars does not match with the dtype the other table's key resolves to

notKnown.name: several-columns-of-a-field-read
notKnown.because: a field read by several names gives several columns, which are no value of one dtype outside a select or a sort

notKnown.name: an-unnest-among-predicates
notKnown.because: an unnest that is one of several predicates of a filter expands to a predicate for each field, or to none, which Polars takes as they come

notKnown.name: arithmetic-on-a-struct
notKnown.because: arithmetic on a struct is done field by field, by the dtype of each field and of what meets it, and Polars does it irregularly

notKnown.name: structs-of-other-fields-meet
notKnown.because: structs whose fields differ meet, which Polars casts field by field and refuses or not by what the fields are
